Hi Priya / Anil —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap from our side and the immediate asks so procurement can move forward with the pilot (30-day, 3-node dedicated pool):

What we covered
- Pilot scope: anonymized inpatient summary generation for two clinics (20k tokens/day expected).
- Timeline: goal to stand up infra and start test traffic the week of 2026-02-02.
- Key stakeholders: Priya (Product), Anil (DevOps), and procurement team for commercial terms.

Open items / asks for procurement
1) SLA exception: MedSys asked for a 15ms p50 token latency SLO for pilot; our standard hosted SLA is broader. We can offer a pilot-specific SLA (best-effort) but need internal approval for a temporary SLA exception and a fallback plan.
2) One-time pilot discount: customer requested a 50% trial discount on usage for the pilot period; internal approval needed.
3) Security questionnaire: you mentioned sending the filled questionnaire — attaching how we expect to consume it and what additional evidence we may need.

Attaching: MedSys_Security_Questionnaire_filled.pdf (from Priya), draft Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (scope/timeline).

Next steps I propose
- Procurement: share a single contact and preferred PO process.
- Redwood internal: I'll loop in Security and my manager for SLA/discount exception approvals.
- Legal: if procurement needs standard amendments we can route the pilot-term sheet.

Priya — can you confirm procurement contact and an estimated PO lead time? Anil — any immediate infra constraints we should plan for?

Thanks,

Rafael / Team —

I reviewed the MedSys questionnaire and flagged a few items that need evidence before we can sign off on an exception that relaxes our standard controls:
- Data residency & retention: need confirmation of whether PHI will be in scope and the regional residency requirement. We require a minimal retention policy for pilot logs and plaintext outputs.
- SOC2 artifact: MedSys asked for our SOC2 report; we can share the certification but I will redact sections and add a short cover note.
- Network isolation: for the pilot I recommend we require VPC peering or a dedicated subnet and ensure key rotation is enforced. That will be a condition of any SLA exception.

If those three are satisfied and Engineering confirms the dedicated pool configuration, I can provisionally approve the security posture for the pilot.

Action items
- Rafael: get confirmation from Priya whether PHI is in scope (one-line).
- Anil (copied earlier): confirm dedicated pool network setup and key rotation capability.
